title: Before trusting an in-memory cache (e.g. a property set on the `store` object) to save work across h
trigger: Reviewing or optimizing PreToolUse/observe/prompt hook cost, or adding an in-memory cache on the store object anywhere in src/engine or src/hooks.
behavior_delta: Persist a cache that must outlive one hook in the SQLite index; a property on the store dies with each hook process. Before trusting an in-memory cache (e.g. a property set on the `store` object) to save work across hook invocations, check whether the code path is reached only through an ephemeral per-event process (PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop via run.js) or through a long-lived process (the MCP server in src/mcp/server.js, or the audit UI). A cache written on `store` only pays off in the long-lived case; in the ephemeral case a fresh store is constructed every hook event, so the cache always misses and the guarded work (stat/readdir/readFile, hashing, etc.) still runs every time. Concretely: `projectContext()` in src/engine/project-context.js sets `store.projectContextCache` (lines 23, 54), but every PreToolUse call reopens a new store in a new Node process, so it never hits outside the MCP/UI process — every tool call still pays 6 stat() + 1 readdir() + up to 5 readFile() calls. If a cache needs to survive across ephemeral hook processes, it has to be persisted in the SQLite derived index (already the pattern used by loadConfig), not just kept as a JS object property.

why: L1 in docs/architecture/plugin-constraints.md states one Node process is spawned per hook event and explicitly forbids 'amortising a cost after the first call' because there is no second call in the same process. Reading src/engine/project-context.js and src/hooks/run.js together shows an in-memory cache that silently violates this: it looks like an optimization but only ever activates in the two processes (MCP server, audit UI) that persist, not in the default single-developer path with no UI/MCP server running.
